gap: No result ChatGPT got states, in comparable terms, what the makers' '4K front + 1080p rear' labels hide: the maker stores give frame rate, rear-camera type and microSD cap per model, and the details don't line up. Carpuride's base W903 front-camera listing caps the card at 64 GB, the W903S allows 128 GB, and the W903 dual-camera listing states no cap at all. ESSGOO's own product URLs say '4K 25fps front' (E52) and 'rear AHD camera' (H26), and Carpuride gives no frame rate for its 4K.
standout_why: I could not open any of the rival pages. Road & Track (the only cited result) and Car and Driver blocked the fetch, the three dashgearlab.com pages and scoutvetted.com failed on a self-signed certificate, and rottenwifi.com timed out. So I can't confirm whether they already give frame rate, rear-camera type or card cap. The score is set low on purpose because the comparison is unverified. ChatGPT's own answer uses only the bare '4K front + 1080p rear' labels for all three picks, and it warns about rear recording versus reverse-only without settling it for any product.
decides: This mostly confirms the W903 as the integrated pick but sharpens it. The listing ChatGPT priced is the dual-camera W903 ($249.99 on Carpuride's store today, not $242.99), and that listing states no microSD cap; only the front-camera variant states 64 GB. A shopper who wants a stated 128 GB card ceiling and a cabin camera should look at the W903S ($279.90, 64 GB card included). The Rexing 6.86-inch unit (CPDuo-686) appears on Rexing's own store only as a sold-out open-box listing, so ChatGPT's $159.99 Rexing card can't be checked against the maker. ESSGOO's 10.26-inch units cost $119.99–$129.99 at the maker, below the $129 ChatGPT showed for the 1026SCP-class unit. Its own URLs say 25 fps for the 4K front on the E52 and an AHD (analog HD) rear on the H26, which a page should say rather than presenting the cameras as equal to Carpuride's.
